key_insight: Factorizing motion recovery into two specialized diffusion models — one in camera space and one in world space — lets DuoMo robustly recover global-consistent human motion from noisy, unconstrained video input while retaining per-frame detail.
problem_solved: Reconstructing accurate human motion in world-space from unconstrained videos that contain noise, occlusions, and incomplete observations, resolving the trade-off between generalizing from diverse inputs and maintaining globally consistent trajectories.
method: Camera-space diffusion model: estimates per-frame motion/pose trajectories in the video’s camera coordinates from noisy or partial observations.
World-space diffusion model: refines and converts camera-space outputs into a coherent global/world-space trajectory, enforcing temporal and spatial consistency across frames.

Joint inference pipeline: the two models are composed so camera-relative detail is preserved while the world-space stage corrects drift and aligns motion to scene/world coordinates (optionally conditioned on camera estimates or pose priors).
impact: Enables practitioners to reconstruct reliable, globally consistent human motion from in-the-wild video for applications in AR/VR, animation, multi-agent simulation, and robotics, reducing reliance on controlled capture rigs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: two-stage flow chart (Camera-space diffusion → World-space diffusion) with inputs/outputs at each stage.
Before/After examples: overlay of raw camera-relative poses vs. corrected world-space trajectories on the same scene.
Coordinate-frame illustration: camera vs world axes and a trajectory curve showing drift correction.
Robustness chart: qualitative/quantitative comparison (error or failure modes) on noisy/occluded inputs vs single-stage baselines.
paper_title: DuoMo: Dual Motion Diffusion for World-Space Human Reconstruction
paper_authors: Yufu Wang, Evonne Ng, Soyong Shin, Rawal Khirodkar, Yuan Dong
